s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with localized tenderness and signs of peritoneal irritation
salient_findings: Localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium
Positive McBurney’s sign and rebound tenderness
key_facts: No history of abdominal surgery, trauma, or chronic illness
Localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium
Positive McBurney’s sign and rebound tenderness
Abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure
Small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right

shortlist.label: Midgut volvulus
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship and small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right

shortlist.label: Internal hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure, and small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right

shortlist.label: Malrotation of the intestine
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship and abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure

shortlist.label: Intussusception
shortlist.why_kept: Acute abdominal pain, localized tenderness, and signs of peritoneal irritation

shortlist.label: Small bowel obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Acute abdominal pain, nausea, and abnormal bowel loop positioning

raw.rationale: The abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship and the abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure are indicative of malrotation of the intestine, which can cause acute abdominal pain and nausea in adults.

rejected.label: Midgut volvulus
rejected.why: While midgut volvulus is a complication of malrotation, the lack of signs of ischemia makes it less likely.

rejected.label: Internal hernia
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of an internal hernia on the CT scan.

rejected.label: Intussusception
rejected.why: The CT scan does not show the characteristic target sign of intussusception.

rejected.label: Small bowel obstruction
rejected.why: While the patient has abdominal pain and nausea, the CT scan does not show the characteristic dilated bowel loops and air-fluid levels of a small bowel obstruction.
